title: MOODBUSTER — Mental health among students
summary:
Europe is undergoing change due to digitalization, global challenges, and demographic shifts. These changes present new opportunities but can also lead to increased mental health challenges. Some people are at higher risk of experiencing mental health challenges. Digital support services that take social, personal, and societal factors into account can help improve mental health.

The planned study is part of the EU-funded international RECONNECTED project. The project is being carried out by a consortium consisting of eleven partners in a total of nine countries with diverse populations.

The goal of the RECONNECTED project is to reach various population groups in Europe -who are at increased risk of mental health challenges - through a digital support platform. The German study of the RECONNECTED project is aimed at 12- to 16-year-old students. 

The main objective of the study in Germany is to investigate whether the use of a digital support platform with various components (e.g., information on mental health, suggestions for mini-exercises in daily life, suggestions for social engagement) improves the well-being of 12- to 16-year-old students and to evaluate which components are particularly helpful. The second objective is to evaluate whether the integration of a machine learning algorithm (personalization) improves the effectiveness of the exercises. The third objective is to conduct a process evaluation to assess adherence, user-friendliness, perceived satisfaction, and potential unintended negative effects associated with the use of the digital support platform.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- mild to moderate mental wellbeing (based on screening using the Adolescent Mental Health Continuum – short form; Keyes, 2002)
- Smartphone with internet access
Exclusion criteria:
- current severe mental illness 
- current psychological treatment or unstable medication
- inability to commit to using the digital support platform
